name: UrbanBites
description: A multi-sided food delivery platform — a Swiggy/Zomato-style clone with a real consumer ordering flow, restaurant partner dashboard, delivery queue, and live analytics.

paragraphs: A multi-sided cloud-kitchen delivery platform — built as a real, working product, not a mockup. Consumer ordering, a restaurant partner dashboard, a delivery queue, and live analytics, all backed by an actual Postgres database on an actual URL.

UrbanBites is a fictional cloud-kitchen brand that cooks six virtual restaurants — biryani, pizza, Chinese, burgers, desserts, and healthy bowls — out of one shared kitchen network. This repo is the full platform behind that brand: the app customers order from, the dashboard the kitchen runs on, the app delivery riders use, and the analytics the business is run by.

It was built to answer a specific brief: "build a Swiggy/Zomato-style clone, production level, deploy it live with a hosted database, for free." Every box in that brief is actually checked — there's a real signup/login, a real order that moves through a real kitchen and a real delivery rider, and a real Postgres database you can query. Nothing here is localStorage pretending to be a backend.
features: Discovery feed — all 6 UrbanBites virtual restaurants, filterable by category,
Menu + cart — adding an item from a different restaurant than what's already in
your cart triggers a real confirmation dialog ("start a new order?"), matching how Swiggy/Zomato actually behave — not glossed over.
Checkout — pick a saved address or add a new one; pay through the mock gateway
